nodes.name: Electrolysis and metal ion separation
nodes.procedure: Chlor-alkali electrolysis of desalination reject brine (DSRB) produces NaOH according to reactions: 2Na+ + 2Cl- → Cl2 + 2Na+ + 2e-, 2Cl- → Cl2 + 2e-, 2H2O + 2e- → H2 + 2OH-, Na+ + OH- → NaOH. Generated H2 and Cl2 are separated. Generated NaOH (LEAN-IN) is split: part used for CO2 capture, part (NAOH1, NAOH2) used in pH swing processes. In PH-SW-1: ~45 mol/h Mg2+ in DSRB + 81 mol/h OH- in NAOH1 → 40 mol/h Mg(OH)2 (89% conversion). In PH-SW-2: remaining Ca2+ + NaOH → 28 mol/h Ca(OH)2 (99% conversion). Mg(OH)2 and Ca(OH)2 separated using Sep models (MGOH2-SP, CAOH2-SP).

nodes.name: NOx capture and utilization
nodes.procedure: NOx in flue gas (FLUEGAS: 0.185 mol/h NO, 0.029 mol/h NO2) captured under dry conditions in absorber (DE-NOX, RSTOIC model) by reacting with 0.214 mol/h Ca(OH)2 (CaOH2-1). Reactions: 2NO2→N2O4, NO+NO2→N2O3, etc., final: Ca(OH)2 + 4NO2 → Ca(NO3)2 + Ca(NO2)2 + 2H2O. Produces 0.079 mol/h Ca(NO3)2, 0.002 mol/h Ca(NO2)2 (90% NOx removal). Ca(NO3)2 separated (CN-SP).
nodes.source_text: 2.2.2. NOx and SO2 capture ... the NOx in flue gas (FLUEGAS) was captured under dry conditions of the absorber by reacting with Ca(OH)2, Ca(NO3)2, and Ca(NO2)2.

nodes.name: SO2 capture and utilization (WFGD)
nodes.procedure: Denitrated flue gas (DN-GAS2: 0.403 mol/h SO2) enters scrubber. Alkaline slurry (SLURRY: 0.004 mol/h Ca(OH)2 + water) from CA-IZ tank (Ca(OH)2 dissolution: Ca(OH)2→Ca2++2OH-, 99% conversion). At DE-SOX (top): SO2 absorption via SO2+H2O→H2SO3→H++HSO3-→SO42-. At DE-SOX2 (bottom, RCSTR): Ca2++SO42-+2H2O→CaSO4·2H2O. Produces 0.403 mol/h CaSO4·2H2O (99% SO2 removal), minor 0.0004 mol/h CaSO3·0.5H2O.

unit_operations.name: Slurry preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: alkaline slurry is generated by mixing Ca(OH)2 and water in the alkaline slurry tank

unit_operations.name: SO2 absorption
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: SO2 in denitrated flue gas is captured when the alkaline slurry reacts at the top of the scrubber

unit_operations.name: Gypsum crystallization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: CaSO4 (i.e., desulfurization gypsum) is produced by centrifugation (W-SEP)

nodes.source_text: 2.2.2. NOx and SO2 capture ... the denitrated flue gas (DN-GAS2) enters the scrubber for desulfurization.

nodes.name: CO2 capture
nodes.procedure: CO2 in denitrated/desulfurized flue gas (DS-GAS: 89.28 mol/h CO2) captured in absorber (CO2-CAP, Radfrac model) using LEAN-IN NaOH (160.6 mol/h NaOH, 7355 mol/h total flow). CO2→CO2(aq), 2NaOH→2Na++2OH-, CO2+OH-→HCO3-, HCO3-+OH-→CO32-+H2O, 2Na++CO32-→Na2CO3. Produces RICHOUT rich solution (76.85 mol/h CO32-, 4.574 mol/h HCO3-, 91% CO2 capture).
nodes.source_text: 2.2.3. CO2 capture ... CO2 in denitrated and desulfurized flue gas (DS-GAS) is captured at the absorber (CO2-CAP) using the generated NaOH.

nodes.name: MgCO3 carbonation
nodes.procedure: Because Mg(OH)2 is insoluble in pure water, acidification is performed, and Mg(OH)2 is dissolved by treatment with HCl. The dissolved Mg(OH)2 then reacts with the rich solution containing ionic CO2, generating MgCO3·3H2O (nesquehonite).

unit_operations.name: Acidification
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Mg(OH)2 is dissolved by treatment with HCl

unit_operations.name: Carbonation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The dissolved Mg(OH)2 then reacts with the rich solution, generating nesquehonite (MgCO3·3H2O)

nodes.source_text: Step 3. CO2 capture and utilization ... acidification is performed, and Mg(OH)2 is dissolved by treatment with HCl.

nodes.name: CaCO3 carbonation
nodes.procedure: The ionic CO2 in the rich solution reacts with Ca(OH)2, which leads to metal ion separation in step 1. Ca2+ ions easily react with ionic CO2 and precipitate as CaCO3.
nodes.source_text: Step 3. CO2 capture and utilization ... Finally, CaCO3 is generated by reacting with Ca(OH)2 ... and the rich solution.
